findings.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.

corrections: Built opposite primary branchlets and opposite flat leaves, with additional paired tertiary leafy branchlets to reduce the bare initial crown.
Replaced a generic spiral cone surface with 24 selected decussate woody scale regions and partial transverse-groove cues.
Retained the same trunk and leaves across small branch deflection, without mature-tree resizing or simulated seasonal physiology.
findings.residual: The crown remains tiered, regular and more open than the retained dense mature photograph. Leaf proportions, bark, lower bands, cone grooves and optics are simplified/unmeasured. The reproductive focus is substantially occluded by foliage in the final comparison; its fine morphology cannot be assessed from that view alone. Deciduous shoot loss and complete cone development are unavailable.
